messages:
Jin Park: FYI — getting multiple reports that the backoffice 'Grant credits' action is failing with a 500. Customer acct_9f3b just hit us in live chat, trial credits never applied and their usage started billing. Repro steps I took below.

Sara Patel: Ugh, thanks Jin. Can you paste the exact steps + any error text? Is this on prod only?

Jin Park: Prod only. Steps: open support console -> search acct_9f3b -> Actions -> Grant trial (7 days, $50) -> click Confirm -> spinner -> toast "Internal server error". No rollback in UI, customer shows no credits.

Marcus Lee: Can you grab the network request and response body from browser devtools? Also check if backend-admin-bot made the grant call.

Jin Park: Copied the request/response. Request: POST /admin/credits/grant {"account_id":"acct_9f3b","amount_cents":5000,"type":"trial"} Response: 500 {"error":"internal_error","id":"req_01Gx"} Also saw this in console: 
```
Error: Error: 500 Internal Server Error
    at grantCredits (/srv/backoffice/actions.js:214:23)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```

Priya Nair: Marking P1 for billing impact. Do we know how many customers hit this? Any auto-grants from promos?

Jin Park: So far 3 distinct customers in the last 30min, but likely more. One was an expired free trial conversion that should have gotten a promo grant.

backend-admin-bot: deploy-record: backoffice v3.14.2 deployed to prod at 1710583000 by ci/cd (rollback available).

Marcus Lee: Noted. The timing lines up with the recent deploy. I'm checking logs for grantCredits errors.

Marcus Lee: Log snippet from prod (sensitive fields redacted):
```
2026-03-17T12:25:10Z ERROR grantCredits failed acct=acct_9f3b err=TypeError: Cannot read property 'tier' of undefined at Object.mapTier (/srv/backoffice/grants.js:88:17)
2026-03-17T12:25:10Z INFO request_id=req_01Gx caller=ui-admin
```

Sara Patel: That stack points to missing account metadata. Could be a null user object after the schema change in v3.14.2. Any DB migrations ran?

Marcus Lee: Migration job was part of the deploy but marked idempotent. I'm running a quick query: `SELECT id, billing_tier FROM accounts WHERE id = 'acct_9f3b';`

Marcus Lee: Result: row exists but billing_tier is NULL for that account. Code expects a billing_tier string. Regression introduced.

Priya Nair: For immediate mitigation can we short-circuit grants to default to 'free' tier if billing_tier is null? Need a hotfix. Meanwhile, can support grant credits via the billing service API directly?

Marcus Lee: Yes — temporary patch ready, will push a small fix to backoffice to default missing tiers and return 200. Can do hotfix if we get ok. Also billing service has an endpoint `/billing/credits/apply` that support SRE can call as workaround.

Jin Park: Please roll the hotfix, Marcus. I have a customer on the phone. If you want, I can run the billing API call for the three accounts while you ship. Account IDs: acct_9f3b, acct_7d1a, acct_c2e9.

Marcus Lee: Pushing hotfix now (PR #4521). Will monitor errors and health.

OpsBot: CI: backoffice/hotfix-4521 passed unit tests and integration smoke. Deploy to prod queued.

Marcus Lee: Hotfix deployed at 1710584640. Initial logs show grantCredits returning 200 for the previously failing accounts.

Jin Park: Confirmed — I manually retried for acct_9f3b and credits applied. Customer updated and happy. Marking as resolved for this session.

Priya Nair: Follow-ups: 1) Add defensive checks in grants.js to avoid TypeError, 2) Add a canary test that attempts grant flow on an account with null billing_tier, 3) Backfill missing billing_tier for accounts where appropriate, 4) Postmortem and customer outreach template for impacted customers.

Sara Patel: I'll open the support incident and draft the customer message. Also creating a billing credit spreadsheet to reconcile any invoices erroneously charged.

Marcus Lee: I'll add the code fix to master and schedule the backfill with infra. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Jin Park: Great work, all. Closing thread once ops confirms backfill started.
